name: Claude Portfolio

targets.name: Merck & Co.
targets.thesis: Steady large-cap drug maker with positive earnings momentum. It is within 6% of its 52-week high and moves less than the market.
targets.risks: Pricing pressure and the approaching loss of patent protection on Keytruda.

targets.name: Nucor
targets.thesis: Leading US steelmaker with high profit margins thanks to tariff protection and a strong balance sheet.
targets.risks: Steel prices could fall if industrial demand slows.

targets.name: Targa Resources
targets.thesis: Natural gas pipeline and processing company whose fees grow with Permian Basin volumes. It swings less than the refiners.
targets.risks: Lower drilling activity if oil prices fall further.

targets.name: CrowdStrike
targets.thesis: Category leader in cybersecurity software with durable subscription growth. The 18% pullback from its high looks like the sector selloff, not a problem specific to the company.
targets.risks: A high valuation leaves it exposed if the tech selloff continues.

targets.name: Marathon Petroleum
targets.thesis: Refiner that returns a lot of cash to shareholders through buybacks and is still 36% above its 200-day average after a strong year.
targets.risks: Refining profit margins could normalize faster than expected.

targets.name: DuPont
targets.thesis: The company simplified its structure after its split, and its recovery is continuing. The stock is up 20% in a month.
targets.risks: Weak industrial demand and costs tied to PFAS chemical litigation.

targets.name: Viatris
targets.thesis: Cheap generic drug maker with improving momentum; it is at a 52-week high.
targets.risks: Generic drug price erosion and the debt it carries.

targets.name: Valero Energy
targets.thesis: Low-cost refiner with strong free cash flow. The 20% drop from its high leaves the valuation reasonable.
targets.risks: Refining profit margins could keep falling.

targets.name: NetApp
targets.thesis: Storage company tied to AI data demand. After a 23% pullback it is cheaply valued ahead of its results.
targets.risks: Its next earnings guidance could confirm a slowdown in hardware spending.

targets.name: Keysight Technologies
targets.thesis: Electronic test equipment maker with a strong sales pipeline; the stock rebounded 7% last week ahead of its fiscal Q4 report.
targets.risks: A cautious outlook in the late-November report.

targets.name: Fortinet
targets.thesis: Third-quarter revenue grew 20%, and it has raised full-year billings guidance three times this year, so the 33% drop in a month looks overdone.
targets.risks: It is very volatile and could keep falling with the rest of cybersecurity.

targets.name: Morgan Stanley
targets.thesis: Wealth management brings in steady fees, and investment banking and trading activity is recovering.
targets.risks: A market downturn would hit both its asset management fees and its trading.

targets.name: Humana
targets.thesis: Its 2027 Medicare star ratings improved, which should restore earnings growth; it is at a 52-week high with low volatility.
targets.risks: Rising medical costs for Medicare Advantage members.

targets.name: Illumina, Inc.
targets.thesis: Beat third-quarter estimates and raised full-year guidance; the post-earnings selloff looks like profit-taking after a big run.
targets.risks: Weak spending by research customers, and the consensus analyst price target is below the current price.

fill_rule: the Interactive Brokers demo account's fills at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday, 16:00 New York); if the broker cannot be reached, simulated at that day's Lang & Schwarz session end, mid +/- 0.05%
rules: Paper money: $100,000 at the start, in US dollars.
Only S&P 500 companies; 10 to 15 of them.
At most 10% in one company, at least 3% in each one held; cash up to 20%.
At most 3 companies in or out per decision.
Claude decides twice a week: Wednesday evening and Saturday morning.
Orders go to an Interactive Brokers demo account and fill at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday); the site records those fills: same shares, same prices.
Whole shares only, as at the broker.
Interactive Brokers' commission on each order ($1 when a fill has to be simulated); results shown before tax and after a 26% tax if sold.
No short selling, no leverage, no options, no crypto.
